seo.meta_title: Who Owns Firehouse Subs? RBI and the Founders' Story
seo.meta_description: Firehouse Subs is owned by Restaurant Brands International, which bought it for about $1 billion in 2021. Who founded it and what changed after the sale.

question: Who Owns Firehouse Subs?
quick_answer: Firehouse Subs is owned by Restaurant Brands International (RBI), the Canadian company that also owns Burger King, Popeyes and Tim Hortons. RBI bought Firehouse Subs for about $1 billion, announcing the deal in November 2021 and closing it on December 15, 2021. The chain was founded in 1994 in Jacksonville, Florida, by brothers and former firefighters Chris and Robin Sorensen, and it is still based there.

body.heading: Restaurant Brands International owns Firehouse Subs
body.text: Firehouse Subs belongs to Restaurant Brands International, or RBI, a Toronto-based company that owns some of the biggest fast-food brands in the world, including Burger King, Popeyes and Tim Hortons. RBI announced it would buy Firehouse Subs on November 15, 2021, and completed the deal on December 15, 2021. RBI's filings put the total price at about $1.03 billion.

body.heading: Who founded Firehouse Subs
body.text: Brothers Chris and Robin Sorensen, both former firefighters, opened the first Firehouse Subs in Jacksonville, Florida, on October 10, 1994. The firehouse theme, the décor and many of the sub names, like the Hook & Ladder and the Engineer, come from their firefighting background. The chain is known for hot subs with meats and cheese steamed before they go on a toasted roll.

body.heading: Why the founders sold
body.text: By 2021, Firehouse Subs had about 1,200 restaurants in 46 states, Canada and Puerto Rico, and nearly all of them were run by franchisees. The Sorensens wanted a partner that could help the brand grow faster, especially overseas. RBI said it saw room to expand Firehouse Subs in the U.S. and internationally using its franchise network and digital tools.

body.heading: What changed after the sale
body.text: RBI said it would keep Firehouse Subs headquartered in Jacksonville and run by its existing management, and it manages Firehouse as a separate brand. Since the sale, the chain has started opening restaurants outside North America. The Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation, which buys equipment for first responders, continues, and the founders asked RBI to keep its mission going.
